title: Our Story
excerpt: How Adakings grew from a single campus kitchen into a family of branches serving students and staff across Legon.

children.text: Adakings began with a simple belief: Ghanaian food deserves a fast-food experience that matches its flavor. Our first kitchen opened near the University of Ghana, Legon, serving students who wanted a hot, generous plate of jollof or fried rice without the wait.
From day one, the standard was the same as it is today — would we be proud to serve this to our own family? That question shaped every recipe, every hire, and every branch we opened after.
A kitchen becomes a community

Word spread quickly across hostels and lecture halls. Customers kept coming back, not just for the food, but for the consistency — the same bold flavor, the same fast service, every single day. That loyalty gave us the confidence to open a second branch, then a third.

Today, Adakings serves the Legon community from TF Hostel, Bani Hostel, and near the University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC), with franchise partners helping us bring Adakings even further across Ghana.
We're still the same company we were on day one: proudly Ghanaian, black-owned, and committed to food made with pride.

title: Why We Built Adakings
excerpt: Founder Kingsley K. Adase on the gap in campus dining that inspired Adakings, and the standards the brand refuses to compromise on.

children.text: Before Adakings, getting a fast, filling, genuinely good plate of Ghanaian food near campus meant long queues, inconsistent quality, or settling for less. We built Adakings to close that gap — without cutting corners on flavor or fairness.
Built on fair standards

Being black-owned and Ghanaian isn't just our identity, it's a responsibility we take seriously. That means sourcing from Ghanaian suppliers where we can, paying our team fairly, and training young people in the kitchen and hospitality skills that carry beyond Adakings.
It also means never treating 'fast food' as an excuse for average food. Every meal is prepared fresh to order, using recipes rooted in Ghanaian tradition and perfected over years, not shortcuts.
Where we're headed
Adakings started with one kitchen and one belief. As we grow — through new branches and franchise partners — that belief hasn't changed: Ghanaian food, done right, served fast, and served with pride.

title: The Future of Campus Dining in Ghana
excerpt: As Ghana's university communities grow, so does the demand for fast, reliable, and genuinely good food near campus. Here's what we see coming next.

children.text: Ghana's campuses are growing, and so is the appetite — literally — for food options that keep up with student and staff schedules. Long queues and inconsistent quality are no longer acceptable when everyone is working around lectures, shifts, and deadlines.
Speed and consistency, without losing flavor

The next generation of campus dining in Ghana will be defined by operators who can deliver fast, consistent service without diluting the food itself. That's the balance Adakings has built its branches around — from TF Hostel to Bani Hostel to UGMC — and it's the same standard we bring to every new location.
Delivery and mobile ordering are now the baseline

Students and staff increasingly expect to order ahead and either collect or have a meal delivered directly to a hostel or office. Campus food businesses that don't offer this will struggle to compete, regardless of how good the food is.

We expect the next few years to bring more campus-focused branches, more delivery options, and more partnerships between local food brands and the university communities they serve — and Adakings intends to lead that shift in Ghana.

Comfortable working on your feet during busy service periods

children.text: Adakings is hiring a Fry Chef to run our fry station — cooking crispy fried chicken, fries, and other fried favorites to our exact standard, every single order. This is a hands-on role for someone who takes pride in consistency under pressure.

Ability to keep pace during peak service hours
Willingness to train junior kitchen staff
